subject: Re: 🔵{Brand} & MobUpps
body:
Hi RECIPIENT_NAME,
Circling back on my earlier email about defending the post-lapse window for {Brand}. With acquisition costs climbing, the 2026 benchmark for health and fitness apps now sits at $30 to win a single paying subscriber, forecast to ease toward $20 by 2030. Against that, recovering a lapsed trialist who already knows {Brand} is a far cheaper paid start, which is why apps like Gymondo and adidas Running lean on a re-engagement layer rather than buying fresh. We measure recovery against a randomized holdout for true incrementality. Worth comparing to your source mix?
angle: fresh angle: rising 2026 H&F CAC benchmark (sourced) + cheaper win-back economics
register_notes: Stage 2 EN health_and_fitness: acknowledges second follow-up and references prior; fresh angle = timely rising-CAC development plus web-verified 2026 H&F CAC band ($30, easing to $20 by 2030), stated as point figures without hedge words; cites peers Gymondo and adidas Running from parent brand set only; MobUpps holdout/incrementality reference carries no figure; one question mark; market context sourced via enrichment_sources URL; native US English; no sign-off; no X-not-Y; no em dash.
